9cfb80b069d364603d4d881ba452943a871ca536.summary: Report on a second stage of the GhostAction campaign, which steals secrets through malicious GitHub Actions workflows. Stage 2 adds a hidden VS Code task and a file disguised as a font that runs a plain Node.js credential stealer and installs a cron job for remote commands. The cron job persists after the workflow is removed. The report found 94 compromised repositories across 66 owners in October 2026 and analysed 79 of them, all carrying Stage 2. It labels the campaign a copycat of the North Korea-linked PolinRider technique, not an extension of it.

hedges: At this time the report labels GhostAction a copycat rather than an extension of PolinRider, since it found no shared indicators.
The report has not retrieved what the server returns, so it cannot say what Stage 3 does.
The report says it did not test two suspected bugs in the infostealer.
The report says how the malicious pushes were made is not established.
The report does not know who ran either push and cannot connect the owner to the operator.
The report cannot tell whether a second GitHub account belongs to the owner or to someone controlling their work email.
The report calls the link between its posts and the operator's changes an inference; it does not prove the operator read them.
The report says it does not know what the date in the batch tag means, or what the server does with the tag.
